rv.q: It clunks a bit as it spins, but it’s also got an endearing wryness to it, along with a pair of finely calibrated performances if not at its center then right outside of it.
Dirty Laundry most benefits from a top-shelf cast.
Dratwa’s moving, clever work unfolded, skillfully and compassionately depicting the messy, difficult business of family relations.
Whatever the reason, she has produced an unusually uninvolving play.
Dirty Laundry was incredibly moving, interesting, and engaging, especially in the way it smoothly crossed genres and ideas.

cn.t: Critics find *Dirty Laundry* a moving, if uneven, family drama. Dratwa's exploration of grief and betrayal earns praise for its clever structure and strong performances, though some find the emotional symbolism too on-the-nose.
